title: `actionLooksDestructive` keys destructiveness off `confirmText` — the exact signal #7278/#7309 are migrating away, and 6 of 14 actions flip
body:
Reported as an `out_of_scope_findings` item by the #7309 dev ([report](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/7309#issuecomment-5256410797)), deliberately not fixed there. Filed unassigned; assign at the moment you start.

No `domain:*` label applied — routing is the triage seat's call. For the record the site is `packages/runtime`.

## The mechanism

`actionLooksDestructive` (`packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts:620`) treats the presence of **`confirmText`** as a destructiveness signal.

#7278 and #7309 are deliberately removing `confirmText` from actions that also declare `params`, moving the question onto `description` — so the heuristic's input is being withdrawn by design, one card at a time. Measured on #7309's branch: **6 of its 14 migrated actions flip from destructive to not-destructive** — `generate_backup_codes`, `regenerate_backup_codes`, `change_slug`, `enable_oauth_application`, `disable_oauth_application`, `rotate_client_secret` — and **none** of them carries `mode: 'delete'` or `variant: 'danger'` to fall back on.

## Latent today — and the reason it is latent is not a property of the heuristic

The #7309 dev established this and it should not be re-derived: the only caller is `summarizeAction`, reachable only from MCP `listActions`, which is gated **twice** — fail-closed on `sys_*` objects (all 14 qualify) **and** requiring `ai.exposed === true` (false on all 14). **Nothing changes today.**

But both gates are facts about *today's platform objects*, not about the heuristic. An `ai.exposed` object — third-party or future first-party — declaring the same shape reaches the live path with a destructiveness signal that the platform's own authoring guidance is actively telling authors to stop writing. The erosion is also cumulative across cards: #7278 moved 2 actions, #7309 moves 14, and #7428 intends to make the pair a *rule*, at which point `confirmText`-beside-`params` stops existing in new metadata altogether.

## ⛔ What NOT to do

Do **not** fix this by declaring `ai: { requiresConfirmation: true }` on the affected system actions. That was considered and rejected on #7309 for the right reason: it adds **dead metadata to a doubly-unreachable path**, which is speculative widening. That reasoning is endorsed here — the fix belongs in the heuristic, not in per-action annotations papering over it.

## Step one — measure before designing

1. Does **any** `ai.exposed === true` object today rely on the `confirmText` signal to be classified destructive? If none does, this is confirmed latent and can be fixed calmly on its merits.
2. What *should* the signal be, now that the platform's own convention moves confirm questions to `description`? Candidates worth measuring rather than presuming: `mode: 'delete'`, `variant: 'danger'`, an explicit `ai.requiresConfirmation`, or `description` presence — noting that the last one would classify **every** migrated action as destructive, which is the opposite over-correction.
3. Whether the heuristic should exist at all, versus requiring an explicit declaration. A heuristic keyed off **UI dialog copy** to decide an **AI-facing safety property** is a category confusion worth naming, and it is the reason this is filed rather than patched.

**"Latent, no change needed yet" is a valid outcome** if step 1 comes back empty and the design question is recorded — but it should be an outcome someone measured, not one inherited from this card.

## Related

- #7278 (ruling: carry the confirm question on `description`; moved 2 actions)
- #7309 / PR #7827 (moved 14; where this was measured)
- #7428 (the authoring-time guard that would make the pair a rule — note its guard must be scoped to `ActionSchema`, per the correction filed on that card)
